newsitem.title: USA: Surgeons replace more skin on Malcolm X widow.
newsitem.headline: Surgeons replace more skin on Malcolm X widow.

text.p: The badly burned widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X underwent a second operation Thursday to replace more of her charred skin, a hospital spokeswoman said.
Betty Shabazz, 63, suffered third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body in a fire Sunday. Her 12-year-old grandson is accused of setting the blaze.

The spokeswoman at New York's Jacobi Hospital said the operation -- one of several planned for Shabazz -- lasted about four hours. The six-doctor team was headed by Dr. Bruce Greenstein, head of Jacobi's burn unit.
"The plan was to remove 20 to 25 percent of the burned issue and replace it with artificial skin. In addition, a second team of general surgeons performed a tracheotomy," she said.
There was no information on why the tracheotomy was carried out. Shabazz is in critical but stable condition.
She underwent a first operation Wednesday in which 20 percent of the burned skin was removed. A third-degree burn is one that extends deep into the skin's underlying tissue.
Once the dead skin is removed, the wound is covered with Integra, an artifical skin product. The material lets the inner layer of her skin heal enough to accept a permanent graft.
Shabazz's grandson, Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, is accused of setting the fire at her Yonkers, New York, apartment.
A judge Tuesday ordered him to have medical and psychological tests before returning to Westchester Family Court Friday.
